title: Parity of the Cosine Function f(x) = cos(3x)
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Determine whether the trigonometric function f(x) = cos(3x) is even, odd, or neither, and justify your answer.

steps.title: Substitute -x into the Function
steps.explanation: Replace x with -x in the argument of cos(3x).
steps.why: Parity is tested by evaluating the function at -x.

steps.title: Apply the Even Identity of Cosine
steps.explanation: By the fundamental cosine symmetry identity cos(-theta) = cos(theta) with theta = 3x, we have cos(-3x) = cos(3x) = f(x).
steps.why: On the unit circle, angles theta and -theta share the same x-coordinate cos(theta).

steps.title: Conclude Function Parity
steps.explanation: Because f(-x) = f(x) for all real numbers x, f(x) = cos(3x) is an even function.
steps.why: Horizontal scaling of an even function preserves its reflection symmetry across the y-axis.
